summary: This defines a scroll-to-top button that's hidden by default and appears when the user scrolls down. The button has a cute animation where it flies up and shrinks when clicked, but that animation is disabled for users who prefer less motion. On mobile devices, the button is made smaller and positioned closer to the corner.

explanations.2: position: fixed means the button stays in the same spot on screen even when you scroll, rather than moving with the page content.
explanations.8: opacity: 0 makes the button completely invisible (but still takes up space and can be interacted with).
explanations.9: visibility: hidden also hides the button and prevents it from being clickable, giving us a second way to hide it.
explanations.10: transition lists which CSS properties will smoothly animate when they change, and how long each animation takes.
explanations.13: z-index: 1000 ensures this button appears on top of almost everything else on the page.
explanations.24: var(--mk-shadow-3) is a custom variable — a reusable value defined elsewhere in your CSS that applies a shadow effect here.
explanations.33: The .show class gets added by JavaScript when scrolling occurs, which overrides the hidden state and makes the button visible.
explanations.40: animation applies a named animation sequence (defined below) that lasts 0.8 seconds and plays only once with forwards, meaning it stays at its final state.
explanations.57: prefers-reduced-motion is a user accessibility setting; this media query detects when someone has asked their device to minimize animations.
explanations.59: animation: none disables the flying animation for users who prefer reduced motion, giving them a simple instant scroll instead.
explanations.69: This media query applies different styles when the screen width is 600px or smaller, typically for mobile phones.
